papers.title: An attention-enhanced hybrid CNN-BiLSTM framework for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition using EEG signals.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signal classification plays a pivotal role in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and the diagnosis of neurological disorders. However, the non-stationary, non-linear, and low signal-to-noise ratio characteristics of EEG signals make accurate feature extraction challenging. Conventional deep learning approaches often struggle to simultaneously capture localized transient patterns, deep temporal dependencies, and long-range contextual relationships within EEG signals. To address these challenges, an optimized end-to-end hybrid deep learning framework, termed CNN-BiLSTM-MHSA, is proposed for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition. The architecture sequentially integrates a multilayer one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for localized feature extraction, a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network for capturing forward and backward temporal dependencies, and a Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) mechanism for dynamically emphasizing discriminative neurological events. Robust preprocessing includes Butterworth bandpass filtering, Z-score normalization, and data augmentation using Gaussian noise injection and amplitude scaling. The framework was evaluated on the UCI/Kaggle Epileptic Seizure Recognition dataset comprising 11,500 EEG segments distributed across five classes. The proposed framework achieved an overall accuracy of 98.83%, precision of 98.95%, recall (sensitivity) of 98.84%, F1-score of 98.90%, specificity of 99.71%, balanced accuracy of 98.84%, ROC-AUC of 99.80%, and PR-AUC of 99.72%. Class-wise accuracies exceeded 99% for most categories, with one seizure class achieving perfect recognition. Comparative evaluation further demonstrated that the proposed framework outperformed several recent state-of-the-art EEG seizure classification methods. The superior performance can be attributed to the complementary representation capabilities of the hybrid architecture. CNN layers effectively learn localized signal patterns, BiLSTM captures bidirectional temporal dependencies, and MHSA enhances the representation of long-range contextual relationships by assigning greater importance to informative temporal regions. The combination of robust preprocessing and data augmentation further contributes to improved generalization and classification reliability.

papers.title: Subject-independent classification of ADHD from pediatric EEG: a leakage-aware deep learning framework with interpretable neurophysiological mapping.
papers.abstract: The use of electroencephalography (EEG) in automated screening of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) has created a large body of literature that suggests promising outcomes, with reported classification accuracies often above 90%. A major methodological issue suggests that a substantial part of these results are actually due to data leakage, whereby EEG epochs pertaining to the same subject end up in both training and testing sets, allowing classifiers to capitalize on features specific to the individual rather than on genuine disorder-related biomarkers. We assessed the performance of three classical machine learning algorithms, namely, Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), and Support Vector Machine (SVM), as well as three deep learning models: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and CNN-BiLSTM, on a standard pediatric EEG dataset containing 121 children and 4,173 epochs. The performance of each model was compared in terms of both segment-wise cross-validation (Protocol A) and subject-wise cross-validation (without any data leakage, Protocol B).To evaluate neurotopographic plausibility without making unsupported causal assertions, we applied Deep SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to the best-generalizing architecture. The performance discrepancy was substantial. Under segment-wise evaluation, the SVM operating on power spectral density (PSD) features reached 90.0% accuracy (95% CI: [89.1%, 90.9%], AUC = 0.96). However, the same model dropped to 65.6% (95% CI: [62.1%, 69.1%], AUC = 0.72) under subject-wise evaluation-a statistically significant 24.4 percentage point collapse (p < 0.001, Wilcoxon signed-rank). In contrast, deep architectures learning directly from raw EEG were resilient: the stand-alone CNN lost only 2.5 percentage points, achieving 72.7% accuracy (95% CI: [66.0%, 79.4%], AUC = 0.72, recall = 88.0%) on completely unseen participants. Post-hoc SHAP attribution identified the highest relative contributions in frontal (F3, Fz, F4) and central (Cz) electrodes, aligning with established ADHD neurophysiology. Hand-engineered spectral features are highly vulnerable to identity leakage, whereas end-to-end convolutional models generalize across subjects with realistic, uninflated performance. Strict subject-wise validation is strongly recommended as standard practice for translational EEG research.

papers.title: Behavioural expression of ictal embarrassment: a stereo-EEG case report.
papers.abstract: Embarrassment is a rare ictal manifestation whose neurophysiological basis remains poorly understood. We describe the case of a 40-year-old woman with drug-resistant focal epilepsy characterized by an unusual ictal semiology combining an intense positive emotional experience with behavioral manifestations of embarrassment. Stereo-EEG demonstrated seizure onset within the middle frontal gyrus bank of the superior frontal sulcus (F2sb), with rapid propagation to the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) and superior anterior insula (sAI). Electrical stimulation of the F2sb reliably reproduced the habitual electroclinical seizure. While identical stimulation parameters elicited the subjective and autonomic manifestations in both supine and upright postures, the complete behavioral repertoire of embarrassment emerged only when stimulation was delivered in the standing position. Exploratory functional connectivity analyses revealed that overt embarrassment was associated with reduced node strength within a network encompassing the dACC, sAI, mesial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC). More restricted network changes were associated with only mild sensations, whereas asymptomatic stimulation produced a distinct and partly reversed connectivity pattern. This case suggests that the behavioral expression of ictal embarrassment arises from the transient reconfiguration of a frontal-cingulo-insular network and is critically shaped by bodily context.

papers.title: Validating electrical stimulation through the somatosensory system: a perspective on mismatch negativity and auditory prostheses.
papers.abstract: Natural touch engages specialized mechanoreceptors, while electrotactile stimulation bypasses them, directly depolarizing a mixed and non-uniform population of afferent axons. Whether this difference in peripheral encoding affects the brain predictive processing remains an open empirical question. The mismatch negativity (MMN), an established electroencephalography (EEG) marker of automatic change detection, provides a powerful tool to address this question without perceptual confounds. Somatosensory studies comparing MMN responses to natural versus electrical stimulation within the same healthy individuals can identify candidate mechanisms for testing in the auditory domain, where such designs are inherently not feasible. In particular, they can help disentangle device effects from deafness-related confounds in cochlear implant (CI) users. Existing somatosensory evidence in healthy subjects suggests that electrotactile stimulation elicits mismatch responses with less bilateral integration than natural touch, though this evidence remains limited to a single magnetoencephalography (MEG) study using an oddball paradigm. CI studies are more extensive and show feature-specific MMN deficits. However, they also rely on oddball or multi-feature paradigms that conflate prediction error with sensory adaptation. This Perspective therefore encourages the adoption of alternative MMN paradigms (roving, omission, or local-global) to determine whether electrical stimulation truly engages the brain's predictive machinery. With emerging multimodal stimulators, the somatosensory system offers a valuable platform to test whether electrical stimulation reproduces natural predictive processing-insights that can improve both tactile neuroprostheses and CI devices.

papers.title: MSANet: a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based driver fatigue recognition remains challenging because fatigue-related patterns are distributed across multiple temporal scales, inter-channel relationships vary across samples, and inter-individual differences complicate cross-subject transfer. To address these issues, a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network (MSANet) is proposed for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition. The framework introduces a multi-granularity patch temporal gate (MGPTG) to model locally continuous temporal contexts, stable graph node enhancement (SGNE) to enhance channel-node features before dynamic graph construction, and an adaptive classifier gate (ACG) to combine cosine-based and affine decision geometries. MSANet was evaluated on two public simulated-driving EEG datasets using a cross-subject transfer protocol, in which the target-subject samples were stratified with a partition ratio of 0.5 into a labeled adaptation subset and a held-out test subset. MSANet achieved an accuracy (ACC) of 83.64% and an F1-score (F1) of 83.74% on Dataset I, and 74.64% ACC and 72.92% F1 on Dataset II. The results indicate strong numerical performance on Dataset I and competitive performance on Dataset II. Subject-level statistical analysis was additionally conducted to distinguish mean performance differences from differences that are consistently supported across subjects. Ablation results showed lower mean performance after removing MGPTG, SGNE, or ACG under the evaluated settings. These findings support further evaluation of the proposed stage-specific temporal, graph-node, and classification mechanisms for cross-subject transfer in EEG-based driver fatigue recognition.

papers.title: Daily regulation of glucocerebrosidase activity and impact of fixed-time rotarod training in a mouse model of Gba1-associated Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the glucocerebrosidase (GBA1) gene are a major genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease (PD) and result in dysfunctional glucocerebrosidase (GCase), the lysosomal enzyme responsible for cleaving glucosylceramide into glucose and ceramide. The pathogenic L444P variant disrupts the enzyme structure and activity, leading to lysosomal accumulation of glucosylceramide and ultimately impairing the clearance of monomeric α-synuclein (α-syn). Given the functional crosstalk among lysosomal homeostasis, the molecular circadian clock, and physical activity, we investigated whether GCase activity exhibits daily rhythmicity, and can be modulated by daily, fixed-time rotarod activity in healthy and Gba1-mutant mice. C57BL/6J healthy controls and Gba1-mutant PD model mice were housed under a 12 h light/dark cycle, and blood samples were collected at four Zeitgeber times (ZT2, ZT8, ZT14, and ZT20), with and without daily, fixed-time rotarod training. A fluorometric assay was performed on plasma samples to investigate the daily pattern of GCase activity. Our results showed that rotarod performance was influenced by genotype-dependent vulnerabilities and by daily, fixed-time physical activity, with overall better performance during the dark-phase training. The fluorometric assay revealed that GCase activity shows a ZT-dependent daily pattern in healthy mice, whereas this pattern was disrupted in Gba1-mutant PD models and partially rescued by timed physical activity. Overall, both the time of day and daily fixed-time physical activity influenced GCase regulation. Our findings reveal a functional interplay between daily biological timing and lysosomal enzyme regulation, suggesting that optimizing drug dosing and timing of administration may improve the efficacy of GCase-targeted treatments.

papers.title: Differentiating linked cognitive states under task demand and sleep restriction: toward an experimental framework for operational monitoring.
papers.abstract: Real-world settings involve multiple interacting cognitive states such as mental workload, drowsiness, fatigue, and mind wandering, yet these are typically studied in isolation. A critical question is whether these states can be empirically differentiated given that they share overlapping behavioral and physiological signatures. We investigated whether task difficulty and sleep restriction produce dissociable effects across these states, and whether their response patterns reflect distinct underlying mechanisms or a common cognitive resource using a unified framework. Participants from operational populations (Study 1: n = 40; Study 2: n = 27) performed three complementary tasks (MATB-II, N-Back, and SART) under two manipulations: task difficulty and partial sleep restriction, targeting cognitive load and alertness. Increasing task difficulty degraded performance and increased perceived workload and fatigue across tasks. In contrast, sleep restriction primarily elevated subjective drowsiness and mind wandering, with smaller, task-dependent effects on performance. These findings provide evidence that cognitive and physiological states influencing situational awareness can be differentiated using complementary manipulations and characterized through distinct behavioral and subjective measures. This distinction provides a foundation for future predictive and monitoring approaches in applied settings.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of emotionally expressive piano performance: a single-case study.
papers.abstract: Understanding how expert performers translate expressive intent into sound remains a central question in the neuroscience of music. We recorded continuous 128-channel EEG from a professional, internationally active concert pianist during a concert-like, uninterrupted performance (~27 min) of six works by Bach, Beethoven, and Chopin. From the continuous recording, 99 two-second clean EEG segments were extracted and assigned to one of six previously validated performance-emotion categories based on independent listener evaluations (Joy, Peacefulness, Melancholy, Argumentative, Tension, Power). Each 2-s fragment contained 1,024 time points per channel, yielding 131,072 EEG data points. Cortical and subcortical source generators were reconstructed with standardized weighted Low-Resolution Electromagnetic Tomography (swLORETA), and activation was quantified both as frequency of occurrence and as dipole magnitude across three macro-regions (anterior, posterior, subcortical). A chi-square test on activation frequencies showed a significant association between cortical/subcortical region and emotional category. Repeated-measures ANOVAs revealed significant region- and emotion-dependent differences in dipole magnitude. Across virtually every emotional category, the left basal ganglia, left thalamus, and left precentral gyrus (BA4) emerged as the most consistently recruited generators, indicating a stable left-lateralized fronto-striato-thalamic axis subserving fine motor control within this performance. Superimposed on this stable motor substrate, emotion-specific modulations emerged: Joy was associated with the highest subcortical activation magnitude, while Melancholy showed the lowest subcortical magnitude together with a selective recruitment of right-hemisphere generators (right BA10, right somatosensory cortex, right insula), consistent with valence-based hemispheric asymmetry accounts. Pearson correlations further linked activation of the left basal ganglia, left thalamus, and left premotor cortex (BA6) to objective performance parameters (gestures per second, notes per phrase, acoustic intensity), suggesting that neurofunctional engagement scales with the motor complexity of the material performed. These findings provide a performer-side perspective complementary to models of music-evoked emotion largely derived from listeners, and suggest that, in this elite performer, expressive intent was instantiated in a specialized, left-dominant sensorimotor-limbic network modulated by affective valence. The study is complemented by animated audiovisual materials that dynamically trace the moment-to-moment evolution of LORETA source activity in synchrony with the unfolding musical passage.

papers.title: Dynamic monitoring and adaptive algorithm optimization of fatigue recovery in track and field athletes based on inertial measurement unit sensor data.
papers.abstract: Sprint recovery monitoring requires individualized assessment because movement mechanics return toward baseline at different rates following repeated high-intensity loading. This study developed Sprint Recovery Adaptation (SRA), an adaptive framework for individualized sprint-kinematic recovery monitoring in 100 m and 200 m sprinters. A repeated-measures field algorithm-validation design included 124 Chinese collegiate sprinters who completed baseline testing, repeated 60 m fatigue-induction sprints, and recovery assessments immediately post-fatigue and at 5, 10, 15, and 20 min. SRA integrated inertial measurement unit (IMU)-derived acceleration consistency, angular-velocity control, trunk-pelvis stability, limb symmetry, individualized baseline normalization, and temporal updating. Recovery categories were defined according to predefined testing intervals and individualized mechanical deviation criteria. Because no independent physiological reference measure was included, interpretation was restricted to sprint-kinematic recovery. An independent endurance-running IMU dataset was additionally used for cross-task feature-generalization testing. The Recovery Index increased from 54.20 ± 8.30 immediately post-fatigue to 86.80 ± 6.40 at 20 min. Athlete-level held-out validation yielded an accuracy of 0.864, an F1-score of 0.861, and an area under the curve of 0.917, with SRA outperforming the strongest fixed comparison model. Ablation analysis identified individualized baseline normalization and temporal updating as major contributors to classification performance. Cross-task testing using the independent endurance-running IMU dataset supported the generalizability of the feature-processing pipeline. SRA provides a feasible approach for short-term, individualized monitoring of post-fatigue sprint-mechanics recovery. Its adaptive use of athlete-specific baselines and temporal updating appears to improve recovery-state classification compared with fixed models. However, the framework should be interpreted as a measure of kinematic recovery rather than physiological recovery, and further validation against independent physiological and performance-based reference measures is warranted.

papers.title: Are sleep quality problems linked to pride in Tai Chi practitioners? Regulatory emotional self-efficacy and years of practice.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality is a central indicator of sleep health and is closely linked to emotional functioning. However, research has focused largely on negative affect, psychopathology, and impaired daytime functioning, leaving less known about whether sleep quality problems are associated with positive self-evaluative emotions. In the real-world context of Tai Chi practice, this study examined whether regulatory emotional self-efficacy (RESE) statistically accounted for the associations between sleep quality problems and authentic and hubristic pride among a predominantly young sample of Chinese Tai Chi practitioners, and whether years of Tai Chi practice moderated the association between sleep quality problems and RESE. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 477 Chinese Tai Chi practitioners with regular and sustained practice experience, most of whom were young adults. Participants completed self-report measures, including the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the RESE, and the Authentic and Hubristic Pride Scales (AHPS), and reported their years of Tai Chi practice experience. Mediation and moderated mediation analyses were conducted using PROCESS Models 4 and 7, controlling for gender and age. Sleep quality problems were indirectly associated with lower authentic pride through lower RESE. The corresponding indirect association was not statistically significant for hubristic pride. Tai Chi experience moderated the first-stage association between sleep quality problems and RESE: the negative association was stronger among participants with longer Tai Chi experience, and the conditional indirect association with authentic pride was statistically significant at median and higher levels of experience. In this cross-sectional sample, lower perceived emotion-regulation capacity statistically accounted for part of the association between sleep quality problems and lower authentic pride. The corresponding indirect association was not statistically significant for hubristic pride. Tai Chi experience conditioned the association between sleep quality problems and RESE, but its direction was not consistent with a buffering interpretation.

papers.title: Time-restricted feeding during the inactive phase vs. ad libitum feeding: diet-dependent effects on weight and metabolic markers in male Wistar rats.
papers.abstract: In recent years, intermittent fasting has become a popular method for preventing and treating obesity and chronic diseases. This study explored the metabolic and inflammatory effects of inactive-phase (Day) time-restricted feeding (TRF) vs. ad libitum feeding (Ad) in rats under high-fat (HF) and standard (S) diet for 8 weeks. Four groups (TRF + HF, TRF + S, Ad + S, Ad + HF; n = 7 each) were monitored for temporal changes in key biomarkers, including TNF-α, IL-6, LPS, insulin, glucose, and lipid profiles, and body weight. Baseline-adjusted two-way ANCOVA was used to evaluate the main effects of Diet and Feeding pattern and their interaction, with complementary multivariate analyses performed as sensitivity analyses. Body weight was significantly associated with both Diet and Feeding pattern after baseline adjustment, with the greatest observed weight gain in Ad + HF and the smallest in TRF + S. TNF-α showed a significant Diet × Feeding interaction, characterized by marked reductions in both TRF groups and little change in Ad + HF. Lipid metabolism exhibited distinct interactions between diet type and feeding regimens. Total cholesterol levels increased in both ad libitum-fed groups, whereas a reduction was observed in the TRF + S group. Triglyceride responses also showed pronounced treatment effects, with the TRF + HF group demonstrating the greatest decrease over the intervention period. IL-6, LPS, insulin, glucose, and LDL-C did not display significant group × time interactions. Overall, inactive-phase time-restricted feeding was associated with lower weight gain, favorable changes in selected lipid parameters, and a reduction in TNF-α. No significant Diet × Feeding interactions were observed for IL-6 or LPS, indicating that the inflammatory findings were specific to TNF-α rather than reflective of a generalized anti-inflammatory effect. However, because food intake was not quantitatively measured, these differences cannot be attributed to meal timing independently of possible differences in total energy intake.

papers.title: Efficacy of acupuncture for sleep disorders in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a randomized controlled trial with fMRI.
papers.abstract: To access the efficacy of acupuncture in improving sleep disorders in patients with amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment (aMCI) and to investigate its mechanisms. Thirty aMCI patients with sleep disorders and fifteen healthy controls (HC) were enrolled. Patients were randomly assigned to verum acupuncture group (VA) or sham acupuncture group (SA) for a 12-week treatment. Assessments included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and resting-state Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI). At baseline, patients with aMCI exhibited aberrant brain activity in temporal, frontal, parietal, and cerebellar regions compared with HCs. After treatment, the VA group, but not the SA group, showed significant improvements in both MoCA and PSQI scores. Rs-fMRI analyses revealed significant VA-related changes in the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) in the left calcarine sulcus and regional homogeneity (ReHo) in the cerebellar vermis. Changes in these imaging indicators were significantly correlated with changes in MoCA scores but not with changes in PSQI scores. Moreover, changes in MoCA scores were negatively correlated with changes in PSQI scores in the VA group (r = -0.536, p = 0.039). Acupuncture could effectively improve sleep and cognitive function in aMCI patients. The treatment-related alterations in brain function may be associated with changes in the dermatome layer and the brain-cerebellar cortex circuitry. https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/mgt/search, Identifier ITMCTR2026000708.

papers.title: Sleep Quality, Dysfunctional Sleep Beliefs, and Health-Related Quality of Life and Functioning in People With Multiple Sclerosis.
papers.abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (MS) are more prone to sleep disturbances than the general population. Poor sleep is associated with diminished health-related quality of life and functioning (HRQOL/F) in people with MS and may trigger unhelpful thoughts and beliefs about sleep. This study aimed to examine the relationship between self-reported sleep quality, dysfunctional sleep beliefs, and HRQOL/F in a sample of people with MS. Participants (N = 200) completed the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), the Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep Scale-16 (DBAS-16), and HRQOL/F patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). Separate multivariable linear regressions were modeled, each including 1 PROM as the dependent variable. For each PROM, 2 models were fit: one with the PSQI score as the predictor and one with the DBAS-16 score. All models included demographic and/or clinical factors as covariates. Two-way interactions between each PSQI and DBAS-16 score and each demographic and/or clinical factor were added to the models. Mediation analysis was performed where each PROM was the outcome, the PSQI score was the predictor, and the DBAS-16 score was the mediator. Worse self-reported sleep quality and a greater degree of dysfunctional sleep beliefs were significantly associated with worse t scores for global HRQOL/F physical and mental health outcomes and several Quality of Life in Neurological Disorders (Neuro-QoL) scales. Dysfunctional sleep beliefs significantly mediated the association between PSQI and HRQOL/F mental health outcomes and several Neuro-QoL scales, and significant interactions between PSQI, DBAS-16, and demographic/clinical factors were revealed. Sleep quality and dysfunctional sleep beliefs are important correlates of HRQOL/F in people with MS. In clinical settings, thorough assessment and intervention targeting these factors are warranted.

papers.title: Athletes and Medical Staff in Elite Contact Sports: a Quantitative Analysis of Use, Knowledge, and Attitudes Regarding Cannabinoids.
papers.abstract: Cannabis use among elite contact sport athletes increases with legal reform and commercial availability. Limited education in cannabinoid pharmacology, use, and risk persists among athletes and medical staff, fostering stigma and reducing evidence-based guidance and communication. Athletes use cannabis but perceive stigma and discomfort discussing cannabis with medical staff. Quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional surveys. Level 4. Two anonymous online surveys were administered to elite and professional contact sport athletes (Canada, United States, Australia) and medical and training staff (February 2023 to July 2024). Descriptive statistics assessed demographics, use patterns, knowledge, education needs, attitudes, stigma, communication, and league policies. A total of 166 athletes (89.7% male, 35.2% aged 18-23 years) and 64 medical staff (physicians, athletic therapists, strength and conditioning coaches, etc) responded. Knowledge (pharmacology, interactions, dosing) was low. Overall, 56% of athletes currently used cannabinoids (81% having ever used), but only 21.7% knew the endocannabinoid system and 67.4% were unfamiliar with therapeutic dosing. Among medical staff, 59.5% were unfamiliar with mechanisms, only 14% were familiar with dosing protocols, and 71.4% lacked confidence in making treatment plans. Of the athletes, 86.5% believed cannabis had therapeutic value, 72.3% wanted education, and 74.1% favored qualified scientists as instructors. Of the medical staff, 79.5% reported strong educational need, with 100% of staff desiring athlete-specific cannabinoid education. Stigma and communication barriers were substantial: 81.3% of athletes perceived public stigma, 66.1% perceived staff stigma, and only 21.4% felt comfortable discussing cannabis with medical staff. Staff believed athletes would be honest if approached; however, <50% believed athletes trusted them enough to start the conversation. Both athletes and medical staff categorized cannabinoids as supplements or medications (unlike street drugs) and both supported legalization and a revision and update on league cannabis policies. Athletes and medical staff exhibit parallel knowledge gaps and strong educational needs amid high interest, use, and significant communication barriers. Evidence-informed education and stigma-reducing strategies are urgently needed. Athletes increasingly use cannabinoids for pain, sleep, and recovery, while medical staff report insufficient training and low confidence. System-level education, communication, and policy updates may improve safety, decision-making, and trust.

papers.title: Sleep in Different Types of Dizziness.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances and dizziness are frequently comorbid, yet the specific sleep profiles across different vestibular disorders remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate distinct sleep signatures in patients with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), vestibular migraine (VM), and persistent postural-perceptual dizziness (PPPD) compared to healthy controls. We conducted a cross-sectional study with 90 participants: 24 healthy controls, 21 with BPPV, 23 with PPPD, and 22 with VM. Sleep was assessed using a multimodal approach: 14-day actigraphy, a single-night home sleep apnea test (Watch-PAT), and validated questionnaires, including the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Dizziness Handicap Inventory (DHI), and Beck Anxiety/Depression Inventories. All dizziness groups reported significantly worse subjective sleep quality and higher psychological burden than controls. However, each disorder presented a unique objective signature: BPPV: Characterized by objective sleep fragmentation and a markedly higher Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI: 31.5) and Oxygen Desaturation Index (ODI: 16). These patients also showed increased nocturnal restlessness (L5). PPPD: Demonstrated a "sleep paradox" with the highest objective sleep efficiency but the poorest subjective perception (PSQI: 11.0). Patients showed reduced daytime activity (M10) and rigid sleep routines with virtually no weekend-weekday get-up time difference. VM: Distinguished by the shortest total sleep time and pronounced, though not statistically significant, "social jetlag", reflected by a 120-min discrepancy between weekend and weekday get-up times. Dizziness is not a homogeneous entity regarding sleep. The distinct signatures found suggest that clinical management should be tailored: screening for sleep apnea in BPPV, addressing the objective-subjective disconnect in PPPD via cognitive-behavioral approaches, and managing sleep deprivation and circadian regularity in VM.
authors: Marco Antônio Sales Dantas de Lima

papers.title: Multi-Metric EEG Connectivity and Graph Analysis Reveal Altered Resting-State Networks in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.abstract: EEG functional-connectivity studies in major depressive disorder (MDD) have produced inconsistent findings, partly because different estimators capture distinct aspects of neural coupling. We implemented a multi-metric resting-state EEG approach combining linear, phase-based, nonlinear, and graph-theoretical measures to characterize frequency-dependent sensor-level connectivity alterations and identify sensor-level network patterns relevant to depression-related dysconnectivity. Resting-state EEG from 30 DSM-IV MDD participants and 28 healthy controls was analyzed using a 19-channel 10-20 montage. After MNE-Python preprocessing, including filtering, ICA-based artifact removal, current source density (CSD) transformation, and symmetric orthogonalization, coherence, PLV, PLI, and MI were computed across theta, alpha, and beta bands. Edge-wise differences were tested using Brunner-Munzel with Holm correction, confirmed with Westfall-Young maxT correction, and summarized using Hedges' g and graph measures. MDD showed frequency- and metric-dependent sensor-level connectivity alterations. Theta coherence, PLV, and PLI were dominated by lower connectivity across frontal-to-posterior, fronto-central, temporal/posterior-temporal, parieto-occipital, and central-to-occipital sensor pairs, whereas theta MI showed few increased frontal/fronto-temporal effects. Alpha findings were more selective, with mainly lower coherence and PLV across frontopolar/frontal-to-central, fronto-midline, and posterior links, while alpha MI showed a limited mixed pattern. In beta, coherence, PLV, and PLI showed sparse robust reductions, whereas beta MI showed widespread increased statistical dependence. Graph-theoretical summaries at 20% proportional density showed mainly lower mean weighted strength and global efficiency in theta- and alpha-band networks. These findings indicate frequency- and metric-dependent resting-state EEG sensor-level connectivity alterations in MDD. The dominant pattern was lower theta/alpha connectivity across distributed sensor pairs, alongside increased beta MI-based dependence. The results provide corrected, effect-size-informed evidence of altered inter-sensor coordination without establishing dysfunction of specific cortical regions or named networks. This framework may support future hypothesis-driven research in independent, clinically annotated, higher-density EEG or multimodal datasets.

papers.title: Prevalence and predictors of in-class dozing among collegiate athletes and non-athletes.
papers.abstract: Adequate sleep is critical for recovery and performance, yet athletes often experience less sleep than non-athletes, potentially impacting their academic performance. This study investigates the prevalence and factors in-class dozing among collegiate athletes compared to non-athletes. This cross-sectional study surveyed 165 athletes and 92 non-athletes using an anonymous online questionnaire, focusing on sleep duration, commute times, part-time employment, and attitudes towards sleeping in class. Athletes reported a higher frequency of in-class dozing (70.4%) compared to non-athletes (55.5%, P=0.009). The primary reason for in-class dozing among athletes was fatigue from sports practice, whereas non-athletes attributed it to part-time work. Logistic regression analysis revealed that athletes had a higher risk of in-class dozing (OR=2.71, 95% CI 1.42-5.16, P=0.002), and both younger age (OR=0.46, 95% CI 0.24-0.87, P=0.016) and insufficient sleep at night (OR=0.71, 95% CI 0.55-0.92, P=0.010) were associated with increased risk. Both athletes and non-athletes are not obtaining adequate sleep, with athletes particularly affected by training-related fatigue possibly causing in-class dozing. Factors contributing to the likelihood of in-class dozing included younger age, inadequate nightly sleep, being an athlete, and engagement in part-time employment.
papers.journal: The Journal of sports medicine and physical fitness

papers.title: Characterizing Cancer Symptom Experiences and Related Psychosocial Concerns Through Chinese Social Media Narratives: Computational Text Analysis.
papers.abstract: Patients with cancer frequently experience complex and multidimensional symptom burdens. Standardized patient-reported outcome measures provide structured approaches to symptom assessment but may not capture the full range of symptom-related and psychosocial concerns expressed in patients' narratives. Patient-generated social media data offer a complementary source for examining how these concerns are expressed online. This study aimed to characterize cancer symptom-related narratives in Chinese social media posts using a conventional symptom assessment framework and to identify additional experiential themes through neural topic modeling. A computational text analysis integrating large language model (LLM) annotation and neural topic modeling was conducted. A corpus of 26,086 first-person patient narratives was collected from Xiaohongshu and Zhihu between November 2013 and February 2026 using cancer-related search terms. First-person narratives and 6 SPPADE (sleep disturbance, pain, physical function impairment, anxiety, depression, and low energy or fatigue) symptom domains were identified using GPT-4o-mini (OpenAI) and validated against independent human coding. Symptom occurrence, co-occurrence, multiplicity, and coping strategies were characterized, with exploratory stratified analyses by cancer type. BERTopic modeling was applied to identify latent themes, platform sensitivity analyses, and temporal distribution were examined. For first-person narrative identification, human raters showed 89.2% agreement (Cohen κ=0.784); the LLM achieved an F1-score of 81.2% against the adjudicated reference standard. For SPPADE extraction, mean Cohen κ values for LLM-human agreement were 0.714 (SD 0.114) and 0.754 (SD 0.095) across the 6 symptom domains. Overall, 13,896 of 26,086 (53.3%) posts contained at least 1 identifiable symptom. Pain was the most frequently identified symptom (5783/26,086, 22.2%), followed by physical function impairment (4153/26,086, 15.9%) and depression (4050/26,086, 15.5%). Pain and physical function impairment formed the most frequent co-occurring symptom pair (n=1407). Coping strategies were described in 7104/26,086 (27.2%) posts; medication-based approaches were most prominent, particularly for pain and sleep disturbance, while social and psychological support were more common for anxiety and depression. BERTopic modeling identified 13 latent themes, including cancer treatment trajectories, health care system interaction, existential distress, family involvement, and financial burden, highlighting experiential concerns that may be underrepresented in conventional symptom assessment. The proportion of posts containing at least 1 SPPADE symptom was similar between Xiaohongshu and Zhihu (53.2% vs 54.1%; P=.35), although individual symptom distributions differed across platforms. Chinese social media posts contained multidimensional symptom-related narratives alongside psychosocial and experiential concerns that may be less visible in structured symptom assessment. Patient-generated social media data may therefore provide a complementary source for understanding cancer symptom experiences and supportive care concerns. However, differences in platform composition, uneven temporal coverage, and the nonrepresentativeness of social media users limit generalizability, and the clinical utility of integrating such data into routine symptom assessment requires further evaluation.

papers.title: [Overweight and lung diseases].
papers.abstract: Overweight increases dyspnea and cough. Overweight patients with asthma experience more symptoms, frequent exacerbations and have poorer effects of asthma medications. In COPD, light and moderate overweight are associated with a better prognosis, whereas severe overweight is not. Similar protective effects of overweight have been reported in severe bacterial pneumonia and ARDS, but not in COVID-19 or severe influenza. This review finds that the beneficial effects of weight loss are best documented in asthma and in respiratory sleep-related disorders.

papers.title: Confounds in Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Part II: Modifiers.
papers.abstract: In the first part of this three-part series, we reviewed the mechanisms that cause nuisance signals in fMRI data. Here, in the second part of the series, we review "human factors" that modulate these confounding mechanisms. The modulators may be trait characteristics such as age or bodyweight, or they may be state dependencies that alter the relative contributions of nuisance signals in the fMRI data. A wide array of psychological (e.g., motivation/arousal, cognitive strategy, task engagement), lifestyle (e.g., exercise, sleep, and dietary habits), experimental (e.g., scanner anxiety, task-related movement), and situational (e.g., prandial state, time of day, menses) factors can affect the brain state directly as well as via changes in systemic physiology mediated by autonomic nervous responses.

papers.title: [Effect of the number of sensitizing allergens on the efficacy of subcutaneous immunotherapy and quality of life in children with asthma].
papers.abstract: To compare the efficacy of subcutaneous immunotherapy (SCIT) and its impact on quality of life between children with dust mite-allergic asthma who are monosensitized and those who are polysensitized. This prospective longitudinal cohort study enrolled 80 children with dust mite-allergic asthma, who were divided into a monosensitization group (n=40) and a polysensitization group (n=40). All children completed 3 years of standardized dust mite SCIT. Indicators compared between the two groups before and after treatment included peripheral blood eosinophil percentage, fractional exhaled nitric oxide, pulmonary function parameters, visual analog scale score, Asthma Control Test score, quality of life score, and Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire score. After 3 years of treatment, both groups showed significant improvements in all indicators from baseline (all P<0.05). The monosensitization group demonstrated greater improvements than the polysensitization group in peripheral blood eosinophil percentage, fractional exhaled nitric oxide, maximum mid-expiratory flow as a percentage of predicted value, Asthma Control Test scores, and quality of life scores (all P<0.05). The incidence of adverse reactions did not differ significantly between the two groups (P>0.05). SCIT is effective in children with dust mite-allergic asthma, and monosensitized children show greater improvements in small airway function, asthma control, and quality of life.
papers.journal: Zhongguo dang dai er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of contemporary pediatrics

papers.title: [Neurophysiological differentiation of children with ADHD alone and ADHD comorbid with dyslexia: a P600-like component analysis].
papers.abstract: To investigate the clinical value of the latency of the P600-like event-related potential component during a spatial N-back task as a neurophysiological indicator for differentiating children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) alone from those with ADHD comorbid with developmental dyslexia (DD). In this prospective study, 66 ADHD children aged 6-10 years were enrolled from the Department of Child Health Care, Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University between June and September 2025, including 28 with ADHD alone and 38 with ADHD+DD. An additional 20 healthy children were included solely as a visual reference for electroencephalogram (EEG) topographic mapping. Behavioral symptoms were assessed using the SNAP-IV, the Childhood Executive Functioning Inventory, the Conners Child Behavior Scale, and the Dyslexia Checklist for Chinese Children. EEG was recorded during a spatial N-back task, and the P600-like component was extracted from Fz, Cz, and Pz electrodes. A linear mixed model was applied to analyze the interactions among group, electrode site, and task load. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were used to evaluate discriminative performance, and 5-fold cross-validation was conducted to reduce overfitting risk. Under the 1-back condition, the latency of the P600-like component at Pz was significantly longer in the ADHD+DD group than in the ADHD-alone group (P<0.001). The area under the curve (AUC) for the P600-like component latency at Pz in distinguishing ADHD alone from ADHD+DD was 0.804 (95%CI: 0.697-0.910). Using a cut-off value of 688 ms, sensitivity was 63.2% and specificity 96.4%. Hierarchical logistic regression analysis showed that model 4 (P600-like component latency + N1 reaction time + age) achieved an AUC of 0.804, comparable to that of model 2 (model 1 + P600-like component peak value + P600-like component average amplitude; AUC=0.805), with superior cross-validation stability. The latency of the P600-like component at the Pz electrode during an N-back task may serve as a neurophysiological indicator to assist in differentiating whether children with ADHD have comorbid DD. A parsimonious model incorporating this indicator has discriminative performance comparable to the full-indicator model, with superior cross-validation stability.

papers.title: Psychological Pathway Linking Poor Sleep to Marital Quality in Middle-Aged and Older African Americans: Evidence for a Compensatory Role of Sense of Control.
papers.abstract: This study examined (a) the mediating role of depressive symptoms in the association between sleep quality (sleep latency) and marital quality among middle-aged and older African Americans, and (b) whether this mediation persisted when sense of control was included as an exogenous psychological resource. Participants were 101 middle-aged and older African American adults enrolled in a larger church-based intervention study aimed at reducing cardiovascular risk. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was used to test the study hypotheses. Sleep latency assessed at the initial assessment was significantly associated with marital quality assessed at the final assessment, and this association operated through depressive symptoms. However, once sense of control was included in the model, the indirect effect of sleep latency on marital quality through depressive symptoms became nonsignificant. Sense of control had direct positive effects on sleep latency, depressive symptoms, and marital quality, suggesting a compensatory process. Psychological distress has been identified as an intervening factor linking poor sleep quality to poor marital quality. Sense of control appears to counteract the negative sleep-induced process by directly influencing sleep latency, depressive symptoms, and marital quality. The role of sense of control as an important psychological resource for resilience has been established in explaining the interrelationships among poor sleep, depressive symptoms, and marital quality.

papers.title: Prevalence of Diabetes Mellitus and Its Correlations with Body Mass Index, Neck Circumference, and Obstructive Sleep Apnea Risk among Adults in Kolkata, West Bengal.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus, a chronic metabolic disorder with the key feature of hyperglycemia, constitutes a significant global health threat due to the rising number of cases worldwide. This cross-sectional study was designed to examine the prevalence of diabetes mellitus and its connection with body mass index (BMI), neck circumference, and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) risk among the adults of Kolkata, West Bengal. The study included 1,016 adults between the ages of 41-70 years, with anthropometric measurements and fasting blood glucose levels recorded. The diabetes prevalence was 12.98% in males and 13.01% in females, which was highest in the age group of 51-60 years. A significant association was observed between BMI and diabetes, as higher prevalence rates were witnessed among overweight and obese individuals as opposed to those with normal or underweight BMIs. Moreover, neck circumference was positively correlated with the prevalence of diabetes. The larger the neck circumference, the higher the risk of diabetes. Besides, the prevalence of diabetes in high-risk subjects for OSA was higher than in low- and intermediate-risk participants, indicating a remarkable association between the risk for OSA and diabetes. These findings draw attention to the need for public health interventions for the prevention and management of obesity, monitoring neck circumference, and addressing OSA in order to reduce the burden of diabetes in urban areas in India. Screening and intervention campaigns aimed at different age groups at high risk should focus on early detection and treatment of patients. The study overall helps in the understanding of the epidemiology in urban India, and such comprehensive approaches in diabetes management are also emphasized.

papers.title: Smartphone Usage Sleep Quality and Behavioral Health in Adolescents: A Cross-sectional Study from Eastern India.
papers.abstract: Widespread smartphone use has raised concerns regarding its effects on adolescent health, particularly sleep quality and behavioral outcomes. The associations between smartphone usage patterns, sleep disturbances, and markers of obesity and vision health have yet to be systematically evaluated in India. To assess the prevalence of smartphone usage, bedtime usage patterns, and their association with sleep quality, overweight status, and visual acuity among adolescents in Eastern India. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 140 adolescents aged 13-19 years attending urban and rural schools in Eastern India. Participants completed a structured questionnaire covering demographics, daily and bedtime smartphone use, and sleep quality. Sleep quality was assessed using a modified Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and smartphone addiction was estimated using behavioral proxies. Chi-square tests were employed to assess associations, and logistic regression was used to identify predictors of poor sleep quality. The mean age of participants was 16.8 ± 1.9 years, with 55% male participants and 70% from urban areas. Smartphone usage at bedtime was reported by 89.3% of participants, and 42.1% reported poor sleep quality. Longer bedtime smartphone use (>30 minutes) was significantly associated with poor sleep quality (χ2 = 42.5, p < 0.001). Daily usage exceeding 2 hours was significantly associated with overweight status (χ2 = 21.9, p = 0.001). A high prevalence of bedtime smartphone use among adolescents in Eastern India is significantly associated with poor sleep quality. Excessive daily smartphone use is also linked with overweight status. Public health strategies should include digital hygiene awareness and school-based interventions.

papers.title: From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster.
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits governing alcohol responses across biological levels. This review summarizes major advances in the genetics and neurobiology of ethanol-related behaviors in Drosophila. Forward genetic screens identified conserved regulators of ethanol sensitivity and tolerance, including cAMP/PKA signaling components, ion channels, neurotransmitter receptors, cytoskeletal regulators, and neuropeptide pathways. Subsequent studies revealed distinct roles for the ellipsoid body, mushroom bodies, circadian neurons, and barrier glia in intoxication, tolerance, and reward. Epigenetic studies further established chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation as mechanisms of long-term behavioral plasticity, while systems genetics and genome-wide association studies highlighted the polygenic basis of natural variation in alcohol-related traits. Together, these findings advance an integrated view of ethanol action and provide a framework for understanding human AUD. Emerging approaches include single-cell and connectomics analyses, functional testing of human variants, and integration of systems genetics with circuit neuroscience.

papers.title: Progress in research on the bidirectional relationship between circadian rhythm and depression: A bibliometric analysis.
papers.abstract: This study used VOSviewer and CiteSpace to conduct a bibliometric analysis of 444 publications on the relationship between circadian rhythms and depression, retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (January 2015 to April 2025). Publication numbers remained low until 2017 but increased markedly after 2018, with the United States contributing the largest share. Ian B. Hickie and Joanne S. Carpenter were the most prolific authors; the University of Pittsburgh and Chronobiology International were the most productive institution and journal, respectively. McClung, Dubocovich, and Logan were the top co-cited authors, while frequent keywords included "expression," "sleep," "circadian rhythms," and "melatonin." These findings underscore the growing importance of circadian rhythms in depression pathophysiology and therapy, with future research likely to focus on diagnosis, biomarker identification, individualized treatment, prognosis, and health management.

papers.title: Additive Effects of Time Awake and Number of Flights on Fatigue in Short-Haul Pilots: Implications for Duty Time Regulation.
papers.abstract: Time awake affects airline pilots' fatigue but it is less clear how workload during that time awake impacts fatigue. Although current flight time limitations take the number of flights within a duty period as a measure of workload into account, quantitative evidence for its fatiguing effect is scarce. Here, we analysed fatigue, subjective workload and flight-associated hassles at the end of 553 short-haul flights from 37 airline pilots. Two linear mixed-models with fatigue or subjective workload as the dependent variable were generated, adjusted for time awake, number of completed flights, number of hassles, prior sleep and pilot's responsibility (flying/monitoring). Results showed that fatigue was influenced by time awake, number of flights and pilot's responsibility, whereas no effect was found for number of hassles. The critical fatigue threshold (flying not recommended) was exceeded 2.4 h earlier when operating four flights compared with one flight. Fatigue was lower but subjective workload was higher when the pilot was flying instead of monitoring. Subjective workload increased with number of hassles, but not with number of flights or time awake. European duty time limitations are justified to include a penalty for additional flights but may underestimate the fatiguing effect.

papers.title: Sleep, inflammation, and pain in musculoskeletal rehabilitation: a structured integrative review of neurobiological mechanisms and non-pharmacological pain management strategies.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance, inflammation, and persistent pain may reinforce one another, compromising musculoskeletal rehabilitation. To synthesize evidence on mechanisms linking sleep, inflammation, and pain and identify relevant non-pharmacological interventions. This structured integrative review examined peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to December 2025, identified through PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and SciELO. Reporting and synthesis were guided by SANRA and EQUATOR recommendations. Fifty-seven studies were included: 24 experimental or observational studies, 17 systematic reviews or meta-analyses, and 16 narrative or integrative reviews. Sleep restriction was associated with changes in interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-α, and C-reactive protein, with responses varying across populations and protocols. Prostaglandins and bradykinin may promote nociceptive sensitization, while disrupted sleep may impair descending pain inhibition. Exercise, manual therapy, neuromuscular electrical stimulation, low-level laser therapy, and sleep-focused behavioral interventions showed mechanistic plausibility, although confirmatory trials remain limited. Sleep assessment and sleep-focused interventions should be considered within multimodal musculoskeletal pain management, while further controlled research clarifies clinical effectiveness.

The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status.
papers.abstract: To examine PM2.5 exposure associations with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults, and evaluate modifying effects of lifestyle and socioeconomic status (SES). We analyzed 10,659 participants from CHARLS using PM2.5 data from Dalhousie University. Frailty was assessed via a deficit accumulation index. Group-based trajectory modelling (GBTM) identified frailty trajectories; ordered logistic regression estimated associations and effect modifications. Three trajectories emerged: "Stable low" (63.95%), "Increased to frailty" (29.00%), and "Continuously worsening" (7.05%). Each 10 μg/m³ PM2.5 increase raised odds of Trajectories 2 and 3 by 15.2% and 12.3%, respectively. Higher SES attenuated PM2.5 effects (RERI=-0.067), while unhealthy sleep duration amplified them (RERI=0.163). PM2.5 exposure is associated with deteriorating frailty trajectories. Higher SES exerts an antagonistic effect, whereas unhealthy sleep duration has a synergistic effect on PM2.5-related frailty progression.

papers.title: Relationship between objective sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese: Results by work in the Shika study.
papers.abstract: Sleep quality and work, as factors related to psychological distress, have not yet been elucidated. Additionally, few studies have examined the association between sleep efficiency and psychological distress, which may affect psychological distress in middle-aged and older adults according to their work status. This study aimed to examine and clarify the relationship between sleep efficiency and psychological distress in middle-aged and older Japanese stratified by work and sex. A cross-sectional study was performed among community dwellers aged 40-90 years living in Shika-machi, Ishikawa, Japan, between January 2018 and April 2020. Psychological distress was assessed utilizing the Kessler 6 scale (K6), a psychological distress scale. Sleep efficiency was measured using actigraphy (MTI-220, ACOS Co., Ltd., Nagano, Japan) that includes the sleep index, and analyses were stratified by work status and sex. A multiple logistic regression analysis was conducted setting the high K6 group as an objective variable. A total of 360 middle-aged and older adults (women = 54.4%; mean age = 63.09 ± 10.48 years) were included in this study. Psychological distress, adjusted for confounders, was associated with low sleep efficiency (β = -0.060, p = 0.013) only among working women. We found no evidence of a relationship between other indicators of psychological distress in men with or without work and women without work. These results reveal a relationship between psychological distress and sleep efficiency among middle-aged and older working women, suggesting that work and poor sleep efficiency may be associated with greater psychological distress. Future studies should examine the relationship between psychological distress and sleep efficiency in women middle-aged and older using longitudinal studies that consider work-related effects.

papers.title: Unilateral nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy associated with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome: a case report.
papers.abstract: This report describes a case of obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome (OSAHS) associated with nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). NAION is an optic neuropathy characterized by painless vision loss, visual field defects, and optic disc edema. It results from hypoperfusion of the short posterior ciliary arteries, leading to acute ischemia and structural and functional impairment of the optic nerve, which ultimately manifests as blurred vision or blindness. We report the case of a 59-year-old Han Chinese male who presented with a 6-day history of blurred vision and visual field defects in the left eye. The diagnosis was confirmed after excluding other potential etiologies. The patient was treated with 80 mg of oral methylprednisolone, which was gradually tapered, alongside neuroprotective and circulation-improving therapies. Following consultation with the Department of Respiratory and Sleep Medicine, he was initiated on noninvasive ventilation (NIV) to correct systemic hypoxia and received bronchodilators. Subsequently, the patient's symptoms showed moderate improvement. NAION is frequently associated with a variety of systemic vascular risk factors, particularly hypertension, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, ischemic heart disease, and cerebrovascular disease. These conditions compromise the microvascular supply to the optic nerve head, leading to ischemia, necrosis, and subsequent optic atrophy. Among these, OSAHS is recognized as a significant and independent risk factor. OSAHS is a clinical syndrome characterized by recurrent episodes of apnea and hypopnea during sleep, resulting in intermittent hypoxia, hypercapnia, and sleep fragmentation. OSAHS is a well-established risk factor for systemic vascular comorbidities, including cardiovascular disease and diabetes mellitus. In the present case, an association between OSAHS and NAION was observed after excluding other potential confounding etiologies. These findings highlight the clinical importance of screening for and managing OSAHS in patients with NAION, providing a rationale for optimized therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Association of insomnia with anxiety might be greater than that of depression among patients with gastrointestinal cancer: a network analysis.
papers.abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancer frequently encounter a myriad of sleep disorders, and these disturbances can profoundly exacerbate their psychological distress, particularly anxiety and depression. Elucidating the intricate relationship between sleep disorders and psychological disturbances holds paramount significance in enhancing the therapeutic efficacy and improving the survival outcomes for these patients. A cross-sectional study including 352 participants from two hospitals was conducted. Insomnia symptoms and psychological distress were assessed. Pearson correlation analysis and network analysis were used to determine the association between insomnia and psychological distress components. In this study, the prevalence of psychological distress was recorded at 45.2%, while the prevalence of difficulty initiating sleep (DIS), difficulty maintaining sleep (DMS), and early morning awakening (EMA) stood at 37.5%, 34.9%, and 46.9%, respectively. The partial correlation showed the strongest correlation was observed between DIS and anxiety, with a coefficient of 0.15 (0.00, 0.23), and no direct conditional association was observed between depression and any of the insomnia symptoms within the network analyzed. Emphasizing the crucial role of difficulty initiating sleep (DIS) in relation to anxiety deepens our understanding of the intricate interplay between physical and mental symptoms experienced by gastrointestinal cancer patients. By recognizing and comprehending these interconnected factors, healthcare professionals can devise more tailored therapeutic strategies, ultimately contributing to enhanced overall patient outcomes.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.abstract: Current practice for normal pressure hydrocephalus (NPH) relies on clinical presentation, imaging, and various clinical procedures to determine the need for neurosurgical intervention, specifically the installation of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt (VPS). This study aimed to evaluate the utility of a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response (over one year) to VPS, serving as an ancillary test to the cerebrospinal fluid tap test (CTT). Forty-one patients with possible iNPH underwent Delphi-MD evaluation of wave form adherence (WFA), a composite measure assessing how closely their TEPs resembled an ideal benchmark TEP. Of these, 18 patients received VPS treatment following a multidisciplinary team decision based on standard practice, blinded to the TEP results. Response to the intervention was evaluated over a period of more than one year using the clinical global impression of change (CGIC) scale, in addition to assessments with a 10-meter timed up and go test and the modified Rankin scale. Responders had higher M1L WFA values at baseline (prior to VPS) than non-responders (median 0.51 [95% CI 0.36-0.76], median 0.14 [95% CI -0.02-0.38], respectively p = 0.012). M1L WFA was successful in distinguishing responders (11/18) from non-responders (7/18) with an ROC-AUC of 0.935 [bootstrap 95% CI 0.792-1.00], p < 0.0001. M1L WFA cutoff was established with LOOCV and produced 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity and 88.9% accuracy. In contrast the CTT result was unsuccessful in predicting shunt responsiveness. This study indicates that higher M1L WFA obtained through Delphi-MD (TMS-EEG), signifies better preservation and functional integrity of the motor network in patients with probable iNPH that had a sustained response to VPS than those that did not. Given replication of results in future independent cohorts, Delphi-MD shows promise as an objective, accurate, and accessible ancillary screening tool for iNPH candidates, prior to referral for VPS treatment.
